title: Steam Ai Game
author: FunctionNice1887
selftext:
So genuine question, I have been creating a video game using Claude. I am a 3d artist etc but never learned how to code other than understanding basics. 

Is it a realistic goal to release a game on steam if it’s 95% coded by ai?, I bug test and have a full team of testers. Plus guiding the ai slowly and making sure features are extremely fun and enjoyable .

People have commented on the game and even said it’s ridiculously fun and amazing. Some people didn’t know it used ai till I told them which I do. 

So is this a realistic goal? I’m about a month in, and before investing money on proper website etc.

Is this possible? And is it something I should continue perusing it’s a passion project with something I have always wanted to make.

comments.body: It is realistic if you are really dedicated I would say. I'm in a process of steam verification myself. And I saw one game being on steam made by AI with 100k Wishlist?

comments.body:

this is one successful AI game launch that I remember: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4084120/CODEX\_MORTIS/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4084120/CODEX_MORTIS/)

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> this is one successful AI game launch that I remember: 

According to the reviews no one really minds the AI part. The game just seems to fall apart the longer you play it.

So we can learn from it that making a game with AI is fine on Steam, but making a bad game isn't. Good for us I guess.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
that game is sitting on 100+ positive reviews and it has been featured by some big streamers. 

that game is already doing a lot better than most of the games in sub even if it falls apart after 20 mins of gameplay or whatever.

like bro, I would brag in multiple sub and take my victory lap if I have made a "bad" game like that.

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> that game is already doing a lot better than most of the games in sub even if it falls apart after 20 mins of gameplay or whatever.

True. Most games posted here aren't even really games, just tech demos at best. What I said is also true though.

> that game is sitting on 100+ positive reviews

It has 104 reviews with 77% of them positive. So no, it's not 100+.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
well, I didn't say it right but still. 77% of 104 reviews being positive (or having 104 review alone) is no small feat. in ai gamedev or manual gamedev

no offense, but I am guessing you probably haven't shipped a game yet. If you do, you would know how hard it is to get a game rated "positive"

as players, we think much of it since we are used to seeing positive rated games. It is hard when you are coming into it as a dev

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> no offense, but I am guessing you probably haven't shipped a game yet. If you do, you would know how hard it is to get a game rated "positive"

I did. Even games with similar rates and even similar review sentiments.

Sure it's nice for the guy to have gained some traction. Doesn't mean that I have to fall into toxic positivity. I'm sure his second game will be much better with the learning applied.

> i have reviewed 25 ai games from this sub so far. 

There's a list somewhere here of the "best" AI games. I tried some of them and none were good. In the end AI is just a tool and it can't magically make a game fun.

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body:
do you mind sharing a steam link? I want to get a sense of your skill/experience so I don't go on assuming more things about you

not sure what is so toxic about it. the guy launched a game and it is rated positive etc. pretty much he made some money off the game. I think that's pretty much what OP is looking for as an example

how old is the list? AIs have been changing quickly i.e. AIs can now open up your pixel art editor and put down pixels for you. not great but Ais couldn't do there easily before. 

I plan to release a list of recommendation myself. probably this week.

comments.author: Familiar_Anywhere822
comments.body:
>I am a 3d artist etc but never learned how to code other than understanding basics.

awesome, well now AI can do the boring bits for you, and do it just as good as a human.

>Is this possible? And is it something I should continue perusing it’s a passion project with something I have always wanted to make.

The AAA industry is full of gate keepers who think they can decide what is a "video game" and what is not.

One great thing about the advancement of AI game dev is the disruption it brings to the AAA space. a Solo dev can now develop whatever unique and novel project they have with little to no barriers or gate keepers.

Don't ask for permission. Pursue you're passion project.

comments.author: PatchyWhiskers
comments.body: Steam allows AI games but asks you to declare AI usage for art and assets. They don't ask about code.

comments.author: MakingAGamee
comments.body: Yes you can and since you're only using ai code and not anything else, you don't have to even disclose that on steam and even if you did, people are alot more accepting of ai code use then other ai use.

comments.author: DudeWithASweater
comments.body:
Steam doesn't care, as long as you have a disclosure that includes you used AI you're all good.

Some customers care, but that's a different issue.

comments.author: EdOfO
comments.body:
It's pretty easy to release on it, no?  
Is your question rather can you make money off of it? Do you have a marketing budget? Then it won't get off the ground.  
Do you have that and good networking? Great.  
Is it unique and fun to play for others? Have you gotten playtesters that aren't friends to confirm? Have you received any criticism you've accepted? No first draft is ever great, so if not, it's probably bad.  
  
How about bugs? Do you have any QA testers to find the bad stuff that happens 1% or 0.1% of the time and you'll never have enough time yourself to find?  
  
But being a 3D artist is a great asset! I find the best AI is still awful at making 3D models, and I'm shite at Blender so it takes me a full day to fix one to my satisfaction. It'd probably take you an hour. And bone animations? Forget about it. No way.

comments.author: EdOfO
comments.body:
Your question is more can you sell it, no? Steam accepts anything.  
What criticisms have you gotten that have made you improve it? Those improvements are the best  indication of something really good being made. Are those QA testers rigorous? Are they putting in hundreds of hours collectively to find those 1 out of 1,000 playhour bugs?
What's your marketing budget? It seems you have a lot of other people involved. Is your networking really good?  
  
You being a 3D artist is already an excellent head start over most! The models these LLMs vomit up take me a full day to fix up in Blender and probably you an hour. Bone animations are also impossible for me.
